title.narrative: BELA Defending Environmental Rights and Promoting Justice 2019-2023
BELA Försvara miljörättigheter och främja rättvisa 2019-2023

description.narrative:
Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association (BELA) har ansökt om finansiering för att utföra insatsen "Försvara miljörättigheter och främja rättvisa" under perioden 2019–2022.
Det övergripande målet med programmet är att skydda naturresurser, försvara människors miljörättigheter samt främja och institutionalisera miljörättvisa. Detta kommer att uppnås genom ett antal åtgärder, inklusive inlämning av nya rättsfall och uppföljning av pågående, kapacitetsuppbyggnad av utsatta människor och samhällen samt andra aktörer, skapandet av en nationell plattform för miljöaktivister, förespråka lagliga förändringar och bredda stödbasen för BELAs aktivism.
Insatsen syftar till att: - Institutionalisera begreppet 'miljörättvisa' och 'hållbar utveckling' genom att ständigt utmana overksamhet, oegentligheter och bristande efterlevnad av lagar som påverkar människors rätt till miljö och naturresurser. - Stärka regelverket för miljö genom att driva på nödvändiga bestämmelser/ändringar i regelverket för att följa principerna om hållbar förvaltning och utveckling. - Stärka miljöförvaltningen genom att upplysa medborgare och samhällen om lagliga rättigheter och skyldigheter och öka deras deltagande i miljöbeslut. - Förbättra kapacitet hos offentliga myndigheter, aktörer inom den privata sektorn, det civila samhället och gemene om rättvisefrågor inom miljö. - Uppnå goda ledningsstandarder och kapacitetsutveckling av BELA samt förstärkning av personalens kompetens för ett effektivt genomförande av program och ekonomisk förvaltning.
Den totala budgeten för insatsen beräknas uppgå till 18 000 000 kronor, varav 1 500 000 kronor kommer att användas för kapacitetstärkande aktiviteter för BELA inom resultatstyrning, jämställdhetsintegrering samt intern kapacitetsutvärdering och utveckling. Ambassaden finansierar 100% av den totala programbudgeten.

Bangladesh Environmental Lawyers Association (BELA) has applied for funding to conduct the programme "Defend Environmental Rights and Promote Justice" during the period 2019-2022.
The goal of the programme is to protect natural resources, defend peoples’ environmental rights, promote and institutionalize environmental justice. This will be achieved through a number of actions including filing of new litigations and following up pending ones, capacity building of affected communities and other stakeholders, creating a national platform of environmental activists, advocating for legal changes, and widening the support base of BELA's activism.
The contribution is aiming to: - Institutionalize the concept of ‘environmental justice’ and ‘sustainable development’ by persistently challenging inactions, malpractices and non-compliances that adversely affect peoples’ right to environment and natural resources. - Strenghten the regulatory framework on environment by pushing for necessary enactments/amendments in the regulatory regime for adhering to the principles of sustainable management and development. - Strengthen environmental governance by enlightening communities on legal rights and duties and by enhancing their participation in environmental decision making. - Enhance capacity of and activate public agencies, private sector actors, civil society and common people on environmental justice issues. - Attain state of the art management standards and capacity development of BELA and the enhancement of skills of staff-members for effective implementation of programmes and financial management.
The total budget for the contribution is SEK 18,000,000 of which SEK 1,500,000 will be used for capacity-enhancing activities for BELA within results based management, gender mainstreaming and internal capacity evaluation and development. The Embassy finances 100% of the total programme budget.

Goal: Protect natural resources, defend peoples environmental rights, promote and institutionalize environmental justice. Outcomes:
- Institutionalize the concept of environmental justice and sustainable development by persistently challenging in actions, malpractices and non-compliance's that adversely affect peoples right to environment and natural resources.
- Strengthen the regulatory framework on environment by pushing for necessary enactments/amendments in the regulatory regime for adhering to the principles of sustainable management and development.
- Strengthen environmental governance by enlightening communities on legal rights and duties and by enhancing their participation in environmental decision making.
- Enhance capacity of and activate public agencies, private sector actors, civil society and common people on environmental justice issues.
- Attain state of the art management standards and capacity development of BELA and the enhancement of skills of staff-members for effective implementation of programmes and financial management.

Selected achievements in 2022:
- BELA's main legal instrument is the public interest litigation (PIL). A PIL is filed for cases relating to environmental degradation in any form which is likely to cause harm to the public, causing violation of the basic human rights, and in particular of the vulnerable. BELA utilises ways and means to encourage people faced with environmental violations to seek legal redress for their grievances. During 2022, 5 (five) judgments were obtained in the following cases:
a. Protecting and maintaining the udyan (park), playground, and ponds of Chittaranjan Cotton Mill, Narayanganj (Writ Petition No. 5739 of 2013) - BELA filed the writ petition to protect the open spaces and to prevent these being sold to politically-favoured individuals ignoring public needs and interests. On 10 March, 2022, upon final hearing, the High Court passed judgment and directed the respondents to protect and maintain the park, playground, and three seven-acre ponds from being sold off as plots. Narayanganj City Corporation is now maintaining these open spaces.
b. Restoration and protection of a beel (large depression) situated in Bijoynagar Upazilla, Brahmanbaria District (Writ Petition No. 10417 of 2021) - The petition was filed to restore and protect a beel in Bijoynagar Upazilla, Brahmanbaria District from being filled up for construction of a private university owned by the local lawmaker. On 24 November, 2022, the judgment pronounced by the High Court declared the move of the local administration to change the nature of the wetland and the purported leasing out of 4.23 acres of the said wetland illegal. At the same time, the court has directed the authorities concerned to change back the land record of the wetland as beel and to protect it in the greater public interest.
c. Protecting Bhairab River from tannery pollution (Writ Petition No. 15782 of 2018) - The case was filed against a private tannery which has been operating since 1980 without setting up an Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and without obtaining Environment Clearance Certificate (EC). The tannery has been polluting the Bhairab River indiscriminately since establishment and causing the adjoining neighbourhoods serious health and environmental hazards. On 10 November, 2022, the High Court directed the government and the local administration to suspend the operation of the tannery until it obtained EC and complied with environment conservation laws. The High Court has also ordered the Chairman of National River Protection Commission, Director General, Department of Environment (DoE), Director (Monitoring and Enforcement), DoE, Khulna Division and Deputy Director, DoE, Jashore to regularly monitor the activities of the tannery.
d. Protecting waterbodies from filling up for implementing housing projects (Civil Appeal No.288/2017) - A writ petition filed by BELA in 2009 to save wetlands from being filled up for two housing projects was abruptly disposed of by a bench of the High Court (the lead Justice is not being given any bench for last two years on allegation of corruption). Although the Court had instructed that wetlands cannot be filled up, it erroneously concluded that the lands in question cannot be declared as wetland. BELA filed an appeal in 2017 with the Appellate Division challenging the High Court verdict seeking clean direction on protection of the marked wetlands (5 beels measuring 112.50 acres). The Appellate Division on 11 December, 2022 disposed of the Appeal directing the Department of Environment (DoE) to protect the wetlands and to monitor that all conditions of the EC (that includes protection of the wetlands) are complied with.
e. Protecting Saint Martin's Island from an unauthorized hotel - Based on the case filed by BELA, the High Court on 20 April 2022 directed the Department of Environment (DoE) to immediately stop all activities of Saint Martin Resort, a private tourist resort on Saint Martin's Island, the only coral island of Bangladesh which is under threat, as the resort had no Environmental Clearance Certificate.
- During 2022, BELA had 53 (fifty-three) pending cases it was following up through filing applications, supplementary affidavits, applications for vacating the Order of Stay, affidavits in replies, extending time of injunction and serving notices.
- As part of the follow-up to secure implementation of judgements and interim orders obtained through various PILs, BELA conducted numerous community consultations in the field involving farmers, landless peoples, fishermen, forest dwellers, youth, small-scale entrepresneurs in rural and urban communities.
- Public hearings are an important means to enhance capacity and fully engage people affected by pollution and other forms of environmental degrations. BELA organised and facilitated 3 major public hearings (in Narayanganj, Gazipur, Barishal) where government officials and law enforcement agencies were present and able to meet and have a dialogue with affected communities on the problem and the possible ways to resolve the issue while minimizing further harm and mitigating conflict.
- Civil Society Roundtable with UN Special Rapporteur on Climate Change and Human Rights in Khulna: On 9th September, 2022, the newly appointed United Nations Special Rapporteur on Climate Change and Human Rights, Mr. Ian Fry, met with civil society representatives and members of frontline communities in Khulna in a program arranged by BELA. This was part of the first country visit by the new UN Special Rapporteur and he heard from the participants and especially the community members about the devastating impacts of climate change and the loss and damage being experienced by them. The discussion centred around four main pillars: 1) The harms being caused by climate change, 2) How the communities are coping and adapting to the changing climate, 3) What mitigation initiatives are being taken and 4) What risks and intimidation are being faced by those working to protect and ensure human rights in the face of climate change. Several issues came to light through the meeting including failing embankments, rising salinity, inadequate cyclone shelters, food insecurity and how women are more adversely affected in natural disasters.
- Establishment of Strategic Alliances on protection and conservation of rivers and wetlands: BELA established 2 strategic alliances to protect and conserve rivers and wetlands in Barishal and greater Mymensingh region. The members of these alliances are proactively contributing to identify vulnerable rivers and wetlands as well as developing action plans to address issues, as well as for raising awareness on conservation of their rivers and existing wetlands.
- During 2022, BELA continued training judicial officials. A training workshop on Environment, Environmental Law and Justice in collaboration with the Judicial Administration Training Institute (JATI) had a total of 68 Assistant Judges and a Justice of the High Court Division. The purpose of these workshops, designed specifically for judges, was to orient the judicial officials on the norms and practices of environmental justice.
